title: Triangulatedness of the finite-level compact-support direct image
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $K_0$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism. Fix a prime $\ell$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and require that its image in $K_0$ is invertible.
Choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and
put $A=A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every object $c\in\operatorname{Comp}(f)$ of the
compactification category [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], the
functor

$$
 Rf_{!,n}=Rf_{!,n}^{c}:
 D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})
$$

of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] is a triangulated functor [def-weil-triangulated-category]: it
preserves shifts and carries distinguished triangles to distinguished
triangles.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary compactification $c=(j,p)$, with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ open and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper. By [def-weil-compact-support-candidate], the candidate is the composite $Rf_{!,n}^c=Rp_{*,n}\circ j_!$. For $T=X,\overline X,Y$, write $\mathcal A_T=\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for modules over the constant sheaf of rings $A_T$, and $D_T=D(\mathcal A_T)$. These are precisely the abelian categories and their unbounded derived categories specified by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; take the small skeleton there inside its larger universe. In particular, the source category of the ringed-site resolution theorem used below is small in the working universe.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: write the compactification and the composite; size convention made explicit from def-weil-pbc-proetale-site

proof.text: The coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ is a finite commutative ring by clause 4 of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The sheaf functor $j_!:\mathcal A_X\to\mathcal A_{\overline X}$ is exact by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], whose statement explicitly includes $A_{E,n}$. Apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to this exact functor between the abelian categories of step 1. The termwise functor $J=j_!:D_X\to D_{\overline X}$ is therefore triangulated, with natural shift isomorphisms $\varphi_K:J(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}J(K)[1]$. This is exactly the termwise factor used in the candidate, rather than a right derived functor of the underived composite.

source.place: Proof, assertion that j_! is exact; expanded using Stacks Tag 015F, derived-lemma-right-derived-exact-functor (Mathlib ExactFunctor.lean:36,80,104)

proof.text: Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to each of the small sites from step 1 with its constant ring sheaf $A_T$. The categories $\mathcal A_T$ are Grothendieck abelian and have K-injective resolutions for all cochain complexes, with no boundedness assumption. The functor $p_*:\mathcal A_{\overline X}\to\mathcal A_Y$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact], applied to the scheme morphism $p$ and the commutative ring $A$. The schemes $Y$ and $\overline X$ both map to $\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ (for $\overline X$, compose $p$ with the structure morphism of $Y$). The element $\ell\in K_0^\times$ has inverse $\ell^{-1}$, and their images in every structure sheaf still multiply to $1$; hence $\ell$ is invertible on both schemes, as [def-weil-derived-direct-image] requires. By that definition, $P=Rp_{*,n}$ is the finite-level unbounded right derived functor of $p_*$ computed from those K-injectives; its separate integral tower construction is not used here. Now apply [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] to $\mathcal A_{\overline X},\mathcal A_Y$ and $p_*$. All of its hypotheses hold: abelian categories, their derived categories, K-injective resolutions, and an additive functor. Thus $P:D_{\overline X}\to D_Y$ is triangulated and has natural isomorphisms $\psi_L:P(L[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}P(L)[1]$. No cohomological-dimension bound and no restriction to etale-origin objects is used.

source.place: Proof, assertion that K-injective derived direct image preserves distinguished triangles; expanded using Stacks Tags 079P (injectives-theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck) and 070K (derived-lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies), and the project RightDerivedFunctor/Triangulated.lean:94-99

proof.text: For the composite $H=P\circ J=Rf_{!,n}^c$, equip shifts with $\chi_K=\psi_{JK}\circ P(\varphi_K):H(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}H(K)[1]$. This is natural as a composite of natural isomorphisms. More generally, the integer-shift commutations of $J$ and $P$ from steps 2 and 3 give $H(K[m])\cong H(K)[m]$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$, by first applying $P$ to $J(K[m])\cong J(K)[m]$ and then using $P(J(K)[m])\cong P(J(K))[m]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite], for every distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow{u}L\xrightarrow{v}M\xrightarrow{w}K[1]$ in $D_X$, the triangle $HK\xrightarrow{Hu}HL\xrightarrow{Hv}HM\xrightarrow{\chi_K\circ H(w)}(HK)[1]$ is distinguished in $D_Y$. Concretely, the last arrow after applying $J$ is $\varphi_K\circ J(w)$. Applying $P$ and its shift map gives $\psi_{JK}\circ P(\varphi_K\circ J(w))$. Functoriality of $P$ rewrites this as $\psi_{JK}\circ P(\varphi_K)\circ PJ(w)=\chi_K\circ H(w)$, the last arrow displayed above. Hence $H$ preserves shifts and distinguished triangles. The notation $Rf_{!,n}=Rf_{!,n}^c$ in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] denotes this very composite. Since the compactification in step 1 was arbitrary, this proves the assertion for every $c$, without invoking a comparison between two compactifications.
